Definition: probably a weight; used as a commercial standard
BiblicalUsage: Abraham weighs out four hundred shekels of silver for Sarah's burial field, and the law fixes the shekel as the measure for everything from the price of a servant gored by an ox to the half shekel every Israelite paid as atonement money. The sanctuary had its own shekel, so no one could cheat the standard.
TheologicalSignificance: The shekel matters because God cares about honest measures. A fixed weight meant the rich and the poor paid the same atonement price, and that is my picture of the gospel: one price, one standard, the same for everyone.
